supportedTask: A reader who searches house upgrade stardew can be given the three Robin farmhouse tiers: current gold and materials, the three-day build, and what each tier unlocks, plus the separate instant refundable renovations that open after tier 2. This is not a choice of final intent.

facts.statement: The newest version section on the Stardew Valley Wiki Version History page is 1.6.15. That page says Stardew Valley 1.6.15 was released on 20 December 2024 and links the Steam news post titled Stardew Valley 1.6.15 Patch now available. The opened Steam post's notes match the wiki section and do not change farmhouse upgrade gold or materials.
facts.sourceTitle: Version History; Stardew Valley 1.6.15 Patch now available
facts.publisher: Stardew Valley Wiki; Steam news post for Stardew Valley
facts.evidenceLocation: Wiki heading 1.6.15; Steam post body beginning 'The 1.6.15 patch is now available.'
facts.appliesTo: PC Steam patch notes as opened. Wiki Version History revision timestamp 2026-05-09T22:46:47Z.
facts.limitation: The captured Steam post text did not include a visible publish date; the 20 December 2024 date is the wiki's statement about that URL. The 40 newest Steam news items retrieved the same day were press and announcements through 2026-07-29 and contained no newer official patch title. That sample does not by itself prove no later patch exists outside the sample. Press headlines calling 1.7 upcoming were not opened and are not house-upgrade facts.

facts.statement: In 1.6 the second house upgrade price changed from 50,000g and 150 Hardwood to 65,000g and 100 Hardwood. Most home renovations also started costing money in 1.6, and that gold is refunded if the renovation is undone.
facts.sourceTitle: Version History 1.6; Carpenter's Shop history; Farmhouse history
facts.evidenceLocation: Version History 1.6 bullet 'Raised price of second house upgrade (50,000g → 65,000g), but reduced number of hardwood needed (150 → 100).' Carpenter's Shop history 1.6 states the same price change. Farmhouse history 1.6 states the same change.
facts.appliesTo: 1.6 and later wiki text. Farmhouse page revision 2026-01-15T18:15:54Z and Carpenter's Shop revision 2026-09-27T07:06:30Z still show 65,000g and 100 Hardwood.
facts.limitation: Pre-1.6 saves and guides still describe 50,000g and 150 Hardwood. That older pair is not the current cost.

facts.statement: House Upgrade 1 costs 10,000g and 450 Wood. It adds a kitchen with a counter used for cooking and a fridge that works as a chest, including for cooking ingredients that are not in the player's inventory. It adds a bedroom, changes the bed from single to double, and allows marriage.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse Upgrades table row 1; Carpenter's Shop House Upgrade 1 row. Marriage page: upgrade the farmhouse at least once. Mermaid's Pendant page: completed construction on the first farmhouse upgrade.
facts.appliesTo: Current wiki farmhouse upgrade table.
facts.limitation: The Carpenter's Shop row shortens the effect to interior size and a kitchen. The bedroom, double bed, and marriage effects are on the Farmhouse page and the marriage sources.

facts.statement: House Upgrade 2 costs 65,000g and 100 Hardwood. It adds two rooms, one empty and one with a crib and two child beds, and the Carpenter's Shop row says this allows two children. The kitchen and bedroom become larger. It unlocks house renovations and building/trim painting.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse Upgrades row 2; Carpenter's Shop House Upgrade 2 row; Marriage page sentence that children require the second farmhouse upgrade and the nursery.
facts.appliesTo: 1.6 current cost, not the pre-1.6 50,000g and 150 Hardwood cost.
facts.limitation: The Farmhouse row says the nursery allows the player to have children. The 'two children' wording is the Carpenter's Shop row.

facts.statement: House Upgrade 3 costs 100,000g and the upgrade tables list no wood or hardwood. It adds a cellar reached from the kitchen. The exterior stays the same. The cellar starts with 33 casks and can hold 189. Casks can be placed elsewhere, but they accept goods only in the cellar.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse Upgrades row 3; Carpenter's Shop House Upgrade 3; Cask page: recipe is the final farmhouse upgrade; 33 starting casks; 189 to fill the cellar; goods accepted only in the cellar.
facts.appliesTo: Current wiki. Cask page revision 2024-10-27T13:47:17Z.
facts.limitation: Cask page also says 125 casks can stay reachable on PC without moving them, and shows a mobile layout labeled 118. Those are layout counts, not the upgrade price. Aging times other than the cask page's 'wine takes the longest, at 2 seasons' from basic to iridium were not copied into this fact.

facts.statement: Robin requires three days to complete each farmhouse upgrade. The Carpenter's Shop page repeats that farmhouse upgrades require three days.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse Upgrades intro; Carpenter's Shop House Upgrades intro.
facts.appliesTo: Each of the three farmhouse upgrades.
facts.limitation: The same Carpenter's Shop intro says she begins construction the day after buildings are purchased, does not work on festival days, and that most projects finish in 2 days by the start of the second day after the order. That 2-day gloss is not repeated in the House Upgrades section. Do not convert the house's three days into a morning-of-day-N claim from the 2-day sentence.

facts.statement: The farmhouse outdoor footprint is a 9 by 5 rectangle. Upgrading it does not change that footprint, so adjacent outdoor tiles are not affected. The interior without upgrades is a 10 by 7 rectangle.
facts.evidenceLocation: Farmhouse opening paragraphs; Carpenter's Shop sentence 'When upgrading the Farmhouse, the footprint of the building does not change.'
facts.appliesTo: Outdoor building footprint versus interior size.
facts.limitation: Renovations add interior rooms with their own footprints. Those are not outdoor footprint changes.

facts.statement: House renovations unlock after the second farmhouse upgrade. They finish instantly and can be reversed for a full refund of the gold spent. The Farmhouse page adds that the expanded area must not be occupied, and that the refund is also instant.
facts.sourceTitle: Carpenter's Shop House Renovations; Farmhouse Renovations
facts.evidenceLocation: Carpenter's Shop House Renovations intro; Farmhouse Renovations intro.
facts.appliesTo: After House Upgrade 2. Not a substitute for the three permanent upgrades.
facts.limitation: Upgrades are not described as removable. A 2023 Steam guide said renovations are permanent; that conflicts with the current wiki and is not a current fact. Version History 1.5 used 'after it's fully upgraded' when renovations were added; the current Carpenter's Shop and Farmhouse pages say after the second upgrade.

facts.statement: Current renovation prices on the Carpenter's Shop page are: Remove Crib free; Open Bedroom 10,000g and 12 more free spaces; Add Southern Room 30,000g with an 11 by 7 room; Add Corner Room 20,000g with a 9 by 5 room; Add Dining Room 150,000g with a 9 by 10 plus 4 by 5 room; Add Cubby 10,000g with a 4 by 5 cubby; Add Attic 60,000g with a 13 by 5 room; Expand Corner Room 100,000g with an 8 by 13 plus 4 by 5 area, also increasing the regular corner room from 9 by 5 to 10 by 5; Open Dining Room 10,000g and 12 more free spaces.
facts.evidenceLocation: House Renovations table.
facts.appliesTo: 1.6 prices. Farmhouse renovation table lists the same gold amounts.
facts.limitation: The Farmhouse table does not repeat every room footprint. Footprints above are from the Carpenter's Shop details column.

facts.statement: Robin at the Carpenter's Shop, 24 Mountain Road, sells wood, stone, and furniture, upgrades the farmhouse, and constructs farm buildings. The shop is open 9:00am to 5:00pm, closed Tuesday, and closes at 4:00pm Friday. The house itself is accessible 9:00am to 8:00pm even when the shop is closed.
facts.evidenceLocation: Infobox and opening paragraphs; Shop Closure section.
facts.appliesTo: Ordinary shop schedule. The same page lists rain, festival, Summer 18 clinic, and pass-by counter exceptions.
facts.limitation: Those schedule exceptions are already the subject of the live Robin and carpenter articles. This fact only fixes where a house upgrade is ordered.

facts.statement: Robin is unavailable for gifting during construction of most farm buildings. She is available during Farmhouse, Coop, and Barn upgrades, and not during Shed upgrades.
facts.evidenceLocation: Gifts section note. Page revision 2026-10-01T16:15:26Z.
facts.appliesTo: Gifting, not a statement that the shop counter stays open.
facts.limitation: The Carpenter's Shop intro says the shop is closed on days she is on the farm completing construction. It does not separately say whether a farmhouse upgrade puts her on the farm or closes the counter. Do not write that the counter stays open or closed during the three house-upgrade days.

facts.statement: Robin sells Wood for 10g in year 1 and 50g in year 2 or later. The Farmhouse notes say buying all 450 Wood for upgrade 1 costs 4,500g in year 1 or 22,500g in year 2 or later, so the upgrade totals 14,500g or 32,500g if the wood is bought.
facts.sourceTitle: Carpenter's Shop Permanent Stock; Farmhouse Notes
facts.evidenceLocation: Permanent Stock wood row; Farmhouse Notes paragraph on buying 450 wood.
facts.appliesTo: Buying wood from Robin instead of chopping it. Selling price of wood does not rise with that year-2 shop increase.
facts.limitation: The 4,500g and 22,500g figures are the wiki's stated products of 450 times the shop price, not a separate measurement.

facts.statement: Paint Buildings is instant and free. Until the farmhouse exterior is fully upgraded, only the roof can be painted. House Upgrade 2 unlocks building and trim painting. Version History 1.6 and the Farmhouse history say the farmhouse can be moved through Robin's menu. The construction menu's move control is instant and free, and a moved building's contents move with it.
facts.sourceTitle: Carpenter's Shop Painting and Farm Buildings; Version History 1.6; Farmhouse history
facts.evidenceLocation: Painting section; House Upgrade 2 description; Farm Buildings move paragraph; Version History 1.6 'The farmhouse and pet bowl can now be moved'; Farmhouse history 1.6.
facts.appliesTo: Separate from paying for a house upgrade.
facts.limitation: The move paragraph names the Greenhouse and default Shipping Bin as starter buildings that can be moved. The farmhouse is named in the 1.6 history lines, not in that parenthetical.

facts.statement: After the first house upgrade, Robin's permanent stock can include the Mini-Fridge for 3,000g, the Furniture Catalogue for 200,000g, the Plasma TV for 4,500g, and the Double Bed for 2,000g. The Child Bed for 2,000g is listed as available after the second house upgrade.
facts.evidenceLocation: Permanent Stock rows with the house-upgrade availability notes.
facts.appliesTo: Shop unlocks, not the upgrade price itself.
facts.limitation: Not required to explain the three tiers. Omit if the article stays on the upgrade purchase.

facts.statement: Moving Up is the achievement for upgrading the house one time. Living Large is the achievement for upgrading it two times. The Farmhouse page says there is no achievement for the third upgrade or for renovations.
facts.evidenceLocation: Achievements section.
facts.appliesTo: Farmhouse upgrades only.
facts.limitation: Not a completion-percentage claim.

facts.statement: A cabin houses one farmhand. Each farmhand can upgrade only their own cabin, three times, through the same Carpenter's Shop dialogue, at the same cost as the equivalent farmhouse upgrade, taking 3 days. There is no option to upgrade another player's cabin or the main farmhouse for them. Cabins chosen at a new co-op start are free; a cabin added later costs 100g, has no material cost, is built instantly, and uses a 5 by 3 footprint. Computer and Nintendo Switch 2 can have up to 7 cabins; other consoles up to 3.
facts.evidenceLocation: Opening paragraphs and Upgrades section. Page revision 2026-03-17T18:25:08Z.
facts.appliesTo: Multiplayer farmhand housing, not the host farmhouse.
facts.limitation: The Cabin page does not say cabins receive the farmhouse renovation list. Do not add that. Related search 'house upgrade stardew multiplayer' is this boundary, not a second article in this pack.

facts.statement: Version History 1.6.14 says roommates were fixed so they require one house upgrade, like marriage candidates, instead of two. The Void Ghost Pendant page does not itself state a house-upgrade check.
facts.evidenceLocation: 1.6.14 bullet. Void Ghost Pendant page has no house-upgrade sentence. Pendant page revision 2026-10-13T17:37:45Z.
facts.appliesTo: Roommate move-in after 1.6.14, as stated by the patch note.
facts.limitation: Do not expand into Krobus gifts, divorce, or friendship. The patch note is the source for the one-upgrade rule; the item page does not repeat it.

facts.statement: After fully upgrading the farmhouse and completing the Community Center or the Joja path, the Carpenter's Shop sells a Community Upgrade for 500,000g and 950 Wood that takes three days and, in multiplayer, can be bought only by the host. A later shortcut upgrade costs 300,000g and takes three days.
facts.evidenceLocation: Community Upgrades Trailer and Town Shortcuts sections. Trailer page uses 'purchasing a JojaMart membership' where the Carpenter's Shop page says 'or the Joja Warehouse'.
facts.appliesTo: Not the house-upgrade search task.
facts.limitation: Opened pages do not define whether 'fully upgrading' means upgrade 2 or upgrade 3. The Joja wording differs between the two pages. Do not expand this into the article. One-sentence boundary only.

facts.statement: On 2026-10-15 the live homepage https://stardewvalleyplanner.art/ titled Stardew Valley Planner – Free Online Farm Layout Tool said it is a free fan-made planner: eight farm types plus Ginger Island, buildings, crops, trees, paths, decorations, sprinkler and scarecrow coverage, seasons, browser save, and screenshot or JSON export. The visible homepage copy does not give house-upgrade prices.
facts.evidenceLocation: Opened page H1 and the sections What is Stardew Valley Planner and Plan Your Farm Layout.
facts.appliesTo: Public homepage observed in ego-browser.
facts.limitation: Homepage marketing copy is not a game-cost source.

facts.statement: In the live planner building list on 2026-10-15, Farmhouse, Farmhouse (Upgrade 1), and Farmhouse (Upgrade 2) are each labeled 9 by 5. Cabin styles listed are Cabin, Plank Cabin, Log Cabin, Neighbor Cabin, Rustic Cabin, Beach Cabin, and Trailer Cabin, each with Upgrade 1 and Upgrade 2, each 5 by 3. The list shows no gold, wood, or day count. A placement note said the farmhouse items can only be placed outdoors.
facts.evidenceLocation: Buildings list of 49 items, observed after the planner loaded.
facts.appliesTo: Outdoor catalog labels, not game prices.
facts.limitation: The first cabin style is labeled Cabin, not Stone Cabin. No outdoor Farmhouse Upgrade 3 or cabin Upgrade 3 row was in that list.

facts.statement: The live Choose map dialog has an Interiors tab with Farmhouse, Farmhouse (Upgrade 1), Farmhouse (Upgrade 2), Cellar, and Island Farmhouse, plus shed, barn, coop, slime hutch, greenhouse, and farm cave interiors. With Farmhouse (Upgrade 2) selected, that dialog shows Married layout, a spouse room list from None through Krobus, and renovation controls labeled Open Bedroom, Southern Room, Corner Room, Extended Corner Room, Dining Room, Dining Room Wall, Cubby, Far Upper Room, Crib, and Cellar.
facts.sourceTitle: Stardew Valley Planner Choose map dialog
facts.evidenceLocation: Interiors tabpanel and the configuration block under Farmhouse (Upgrade 2), 2026-10-15.
facts.appliesTo: Planner labels only.
facts.limitation: The renovation checkboxes were visible and were not toggled, so this fact does not say the drawn rooms match wiki footprints. Planner names Far Upper Room, Dining Room Wall, and Crib are not the wiki names Add Attic, Open Dining Room, and Remove Crib. The planner showed no renovation prices.

facts.statement: Google was opened at https://www.google.com/search?q=house+upgrade+stardew&hl=en&gl=us&pws=0&num=10. documentElement.lang was en. The footer text was 'Results are not personalized' and 'United States - From your IP address'. No People Also Ask block was in the captured result text.
facts.sourceTitle: Google Search results for house upgrade stardew
facts.evidenceLocation: sources/serp-google-house-upgrade-stardew.txt footer.
facts.appliesTo: This query, this browser session, country-level United States.
facts.limitation: The receipt names the United States, not a city. It is not a city-targeted SERP. An extension added AITDK and SiteData blocks between results; the organic links were still readable. Result counts and AI Overview text are not facts.

facts.statement: The same Google page listed People also search for: Full house upgrade Stardew; Best house upgrade stardew; 2nd house upgrade Stardew; House upgrade Stardew Valley cost; House upgrade stardew multiplayer; 3rd house upgrade Stardew; House upgrade Stardew requirements; 1st house upgrade Stardew.
facts.sourceTitle: Google Search results for house upgrade stardew
facts.evidenceLocation: People also search for block in the saved SERP text.
facts.appliesTo: Related searches on this SERP, not PAA answers.
facts.limitation: These are queries, not verified answers. PAA was not present and is not invented.

facts.statement: The live page https://stardewvalleyplanner.art/carpenter-stardew returned H1 'Carpenter Stardew Valley: Robin’s Shop, Buildings, and Upgrades'. Its on-page contents include 'Compare farmhouse upgrades with outdoor construction' and do not present the 10,000g, 65,000g, or 100,000g tier table. The live blog index has no separate house-upgrade article.
facts.sourceTitle: Carpenter Stardew Valley article and blog index
facts.evidenceLocation: Opened English pages on 2026-10-15. html lang=en.
facts.appliesTo: Existing English carpenter article versus this keyword.
facts.limitation: Overlap is the decision to use Robin for a house change versus an outdoor building. The cost, material, day, and renovation-price task is not already on that page. Do not overwrite the URL.

facts.statement: The live English blog index Latest articles block, opened 2026-10-15, listed first: How to Harvest Stardew Valley Crops by Hand, Scythe, or Axe; Stardew Valley Oak Tree vs Maple: The Seed or the Tapper Product Names the Tree; Stardew Fruit: Find Its Source Before Buying Seeds. Each URL returned that H1.
facts.evidenceLocation: Latest articles on /blog, then /how-to-harvest-stardew-valley, /oak-tree-vs-maple-stardew, and /stardew-fruit.
facts.appliesTo: Title-pattern check only.
facts.limitation: The cards show author and read time, not a calendar date. Git addition dates in this checkout are 2026-10-13, 2026-09-27, and 2026-09-26 for those three files. None is a house-upgrade task.

facts.statement: The local file media-research/inspected/steam-robin-menu.png shows Robin's dialogue with the lines Shop, Upgrade House, Construct Farm Buildings, and Leave. The image shows no upgrade price, material count, or day count, and it has no version label.
facts.evidenceLocation: Dialogue box in the PNG.
facts.appliesTo: Menu labels only.
facts.limitation: Not a price source. License text in the media-research notes was not used. Exterior and cellar PNGs in originals/ show buildings or casks and no prices; they were not used to count casks or to claim upgrade 3 has a unique exterior.

facts.statement: The Steam guide ranked second was opened at the SERP URL with l=german. Chrome lang was de, the guide body is English, and the page shows published and updated 21 Dec 2023. Its upgrade 2 line says 50,000 Gold and 150 Hardwood, and it calls renovations permanent. That contradicts the current wiki.
facts.evidenceLocation: Upgrade table and the note under it; date line 21. Dez. 2023.
facts.appliesTo: SERP type evidence only.
facts.limitation: Do not use its costs or its permanent-renovation sentence as current facts. A YouTube snippet on the same SERP, not opened, also said 50k for a middle tier. Not used.

facts.statement: The opened top results and the related searches about 1st, 2nd, 3rd, cost, and requirements support a tier-cost-and-unlock task. Renovation versus upgrade is required inside that task because tier 2 unlocks a different, instant, refundable menu. The Reddit thread is an opinion about whether to spend, not a cost source. Cabin multiplayer and the community upgrade stay one-sentence boundaries.
facts.evidenceLocation: OBS-serp, OBS-related-searches, T-upgrade-1, T-upgrade-2, T-upgrade-3, T-renovation-rule.
facts.appliesTo: Candidate for B. Not a selected intent.
facts.limitation: B chooses the final intent. A does not write the outline, title, or body.

facts.statement: There is no core blocker for the tier costs, materials, three-day builds, marriage and nursery unlocks, cellar, 1.6 price change, or renovation-versus-upgrade distinction. Unresolved items are the community-upgrade word 'fully', whether the shop counter is open during the three house days, a city name on the US SERP, and a publish date printed on the Steam 1.6.15 post itself.
facts.evidenceLocation: T-days limitation, T-gifting-exception limitation, T-community-boundary, T-version limitation, OBS-serp limitation.
facts.appliesTo: Handoff to B.
facts.limitation: If B writes the counter status or the community upgrade tier, those claims are not supported yet.
